summary.notes: Healthcare mandate: prefers-reduced-motion is a legal requirement (WCAG 2.1 AA). All critical findings in the missing-reduced-motion category must be remediated before any release.

findings.description: Base .button element has 4 transition properties (background-color, color, border-color, box-shadow) but the @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block on line 173 only covers .button__spinner. The base button transitions are never disabled for users who prefer reduced motion.
.alert__close-button has transition on opacity and background-color but no @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block covers it.
.link has transitions on color, text-decoration-color, and box-shadow but there is NO @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block anywhere in the file. Complete omission.
.divider has a transition on background-color but there is NO @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block anywhere in the file. Complete omission.
.meter__indicator transitions width but there is NO @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block anywhere in the file. Complete omission.

.step__indicator has transitions on background-color, border-color, and color (lines 67-70), and .step__connector has transition on background-color (line 87), but there is NO @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block anywhere in the file. Complete omission.

.code-snippet__copy-button has transitions on background-color, color, and opacity (lines 89-92), and .code-snippet__expand-button has transition on color (line 128), but there is NO @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block anywhere in the file. Complete omission.
.field__textarea-wrapper has transitions on border-color and box-shadow but there is NO @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block covering it.

.dialog__close-btn has transitions on background-color and opacity (lines 131-133) but these are NOT covered by the existing @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block which only covers .dialog__backdrop and .dialog__panel.
.drawer-close-button has transition on opacity (line 200) but this is NOT covered by the existing @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block which only covers .drawer-backdrop and .drawer-panel.
.toast__close has transition on opacity (line 132) but this is NOT covered by the existing @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block which only covers .toast.

.menu-item has transition on background-color (line 30) and .menu-item__checked-icon has transition on opacity (line 61), but the @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block only covers .menu-item__spinner. The base item and checked icon transitions are never disabled.

tbody tr has transition on background-color (line 128), and .sort-icon has transitions on opacity and transform (lines 111-113), but the @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block only covers .skeleton__shimmer. Table row hover and sort icon animations are never disabled.

.side-nav__toggle has transition on background-color and color (lines 95-97) but is NOT covered by the existing @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block which covers .side-nav and .side-nav__toggle svg.

Multiple elements have transitions not covered by the reduced-motion block: .field__trigger (line 129), .calendar__nav-btn (lines 214-216), and .calendar__day (lines 288-290). The existing prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference block on line 172 only handles the calendar slide animation.
.field__clear-button (line 157) and .field__chip-remove (line 385) have transitions not covered by the existing @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block.
findings.current:
.field__clear-button { transition: color ..., opacity ...; }
.field__chip-remove { transition: color ..., opacity ...; }

findings.description: .field__combobox has transitions on border-color and box-shadow (lines 52-54) and .field__option has transition on background-color (line 191), but only the listbox animation is gated behind prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference. These element transitions have no reduced-motion coverage.

.progress-bar__fill transitions width which triggers layout recalculation on every frame. This is not GPU-compositable. The indeterminate @keyframes (lines 84-95) also animate width. Use transform: scaleX() instead for 60fps.
.nav-item__label transitions width (line 115) which triggers layout. .nav-item__children transitions max-height (line 156) which also triggers layout. Both should use compositable properties.
.progress-bar transitions width which triggers layout recalculation. Use transform: scaleX() for GPU-compositable animation.
.slider__fill transitions width which triggers layout recalculation on every frame during drag. Use transform: scaleX() for smooth 60fps fills.
.meter__indicator transitions width which triggers layout recalculation. Use transform: scaleX() for GPU-compositable animation.
Hardcoded timing values 0.15s ease used for opacity and visibility transitions instead of design token --hx-transition-fast.
Hardcoded animation duration 1.5s on hx-spinner-dash keyframe instead of using a design token for animation timing.
Hardcoded timing 0.2s ease on .progress-bar__fill transition instead of using design token --hx-transition-normal.
Hardcoded timing 0.15s ease on .divider background-color transition instead of using design token --hx-transition-fast.
Uses --hx-tooltip-transition-duration with hardcoded fallback 0.15s. While partially tokenized, the fallback should reference --hx-transition-fast timing for consistency.
Uses --hx-popover-transition-duration with hardcoded fallback 0.2s. While partially tokenized, the fallback should reference a standard motion token.
Focus ring uses hardcoded 2px solid var(--hx-color-primary-500) without --hx-focus-ring-width token, inconsistent with all other components.

Interactive list items have transition on background-color (line 34) but there is no @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block in the file. While this is a subtle hover transition, the reduced-motion pattern should be present for completeness.
Uses bare ease on hardcoded 0.2s while indeterminate animation uses ease-in-out. Inconsistent easing curves within the same component.
findings.current:
.progress-bar__fill { transition: width 0.2s ease; }
@keyframes progress-bar-indeterminate { animation: ... ease-in-out; }
findings.fix: Standardize on ease or use --hx-easing-standard token for both.

findings.description: Uses three different easing functions: linear (rotate), ease-in-out (dash), and implicit ease across animations. While intentional for spinner physics, this should be documented.
findings.current:
animation: hx-spinner-rotate 2s linear infinite;
animation: hx-spinner-dash 1.5s ease-in-out infinite;
findings.fix: No code change needed — add CSS comment explaining intentional easing choices for rotate vs dash physics.

findings.description: The .collapse-btn elements (lines 133-148) have hardcoded 20px width/height and hardcoded 8px font-size without CSS custom properties for consumer override. No CSS parts exposed for the collapse controls.
Collapse controls use hardcoded gap: 4px (line 125) instead of a design token.
The indeterminate animation duration uses hardcoded 1.5s in @keyframes without a CSS custom property for consumer control.
.field__chip-remove has transitions on color and opacity but is not covered by existing reduced-motion block. This is a secondary finding to CMA-016 but specific to the chip removal button.
Indeterminate animation uses hardcoded 1.5s duration and 0.6s delay without design tokens.
Shimmer animation uses hardcoded 1.5s duration without a design token for consumer control.
Pulse animation uses hardcoded 2s duration without a design token.
Pulse animation uses hardcoded duration without a design token.
Track scroll-behavior uses hardcoded smooth without a way to control scroll duration/easing via token. Nav buttons use tokens correctly.
findings.fix: No direct CSS fix for scroll-behavior timing. Document that scroll-behavior: smooth duration is browser-controlled. The existing prefers-reduced-motion: reduce correctly disables this.

findings.description: .collapse-controls uses hardcoded z-index: 2 without a design token. While this is within shadow DOM scope and unlikely to cause stacking issues, it should use a token for consistency.
Focus-within uses z-index: 1. While correctly scoped within shadow DOM and documented with a comment, it uses a hardcoded value.
findings.fix: Acceptable as-is. The z-index: 1 is locally scoped and well-documented. Low priority.

findings.description: .toast animates both opacity and transform on show/hide but does not use will-change to hint GPU layer promotion. For frequently appearing/disappearing toasts, this could improve initial animation frame.
.dialog__panel animates opacity and transform on open/close but does not hint will-change. Dialog open is a user-initiated action where a single dropped frame is noticeable.
.drawer-panel animates transform on open/close but does not hint will-change. Drawer slide animation benefits from GPU layer promotion.

hx-step has a @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) block but it only covers .step__connector-line. Other elements like .step__indicator, .step__label, and .step__description use hardcoded light-mode fallback colors without dark mode overrides.

hx-table has a @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) block but this is the only component with explicit dark mode styles. The library should either consistently provide dark mode via design tokens at the theme level, or all components should have dark mode blocks. Current state creates an inconsistent experience.
findings.fix: Strategy decision: either remove component-level dark mode from hx-table and handle all dark mode at the hx-theme token level, OR add @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) blocks to all components. Token-level approach is recommended for maintainability.

findings.description: .collapse-btn uses hardcoded border: 2px solid var(--hx-color-neutral-0) without a token for border width.
Focus-visible on .divider uses box-shadow with hardcoded 4px spread and 30% alpha via color-mix. These values should be tokenized.
Uses display: inline which is correct for an inline formatting component. No issue — included for audit completeness. All components have :host display defined.
findings.fix: No fix needed. All components correctly define :host display.

findings.description: The determinate .progress-bar__fill has transition: width 0.2s ease but the @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block only covers the indeterminate animation. The determinate fill transition is never disabled.

immediate: Fix all 17 critical missing-reduced-motion findings (CMA-001 through CMA-017). This is a healthcare legal mandate under WCAG 2.1 AA.

Audit pattern: most components miss close/remove button transitions in their reduced-motion blocks. Establish a checklist: every element with a transition or animation MUST appear in the reduced-motion block.
high_priority: Replace width transitions with transform: scaleX() in progress bars, sliders, meters, and file upload (CMA-018 through CMA-022). These cause layout thrashing and can drop below 60fps.
For hx-nav-item children expand/collapse, adopt the CSS grid 0fr/1fr pattern already proven in hx-accordion-item and hx-tree-item.
medium_priority: Replace all hardcoded timing values with --hx-transition-* tokens (CMA-023 through CMA-041). Create component-specific animation duration tokens where needed.
Resolve the dark mode strategy: either remove the one-off dark mode from hx-table/hx-step or propagate consistently via hx-theme token overrides.
Tokenize hardcoded values in hx-split-panel collapse controls (sizes, gaps, borders).
low_priority: Add will-change hints to overlay components (toast, dialog, drawer) for smoother initial animation frames.
Document intentional easing differences in spinner component.
The z-index values within shadow DOM are well-scoped and low risk.
